observations.disposition_note: The settlement and the resulting $5.45M loan payable are one reported event in one sentence; splitting would not add checkability.
This is an inference finding; the cited passages supply the premises (a cross-reference plus matching amount, date and gain), not an explicit statement.
I read the full surrounding context in s0201, s0207 and s0210. The Note 11 table's Atrium row ($4,802,445) matches this loan's stated balance.
The economic role is a contingent default trigger (a funding constraint), not a scheduled cash obligation. I use it only as a constraint.
Marked is_inference. The premises are the matching $2,920,824 balance and a zero Dec 31, 2023 balance for both; the name link is not stated in the text.
Section 4.1.1 is a single repayment clause that sets out tiered minimums; I keep it whole so the payment rule is not misread.
The parenthetical loan terms only identify the loan; the one checkable claim is the $93,736 balance.
It is the opening-cash observation for the model (a cash pool), not a restriction. It is used as the approximate opening balance.
The draws and the partial repayment on the same note in the same period are one reported subsequent event; the net activity is what matters.
The 'short-term' descriptor matches the same table's 'Short term loan payable, related party (1,181,222)' line; the one claim is the balance.
Amount and purpose describe one restricted balance; this is one claim.
'Paid in full' logically entails no remaining payment; this is one claim restated.
It is one recommended disposition of a single motion, quoted verbatim; splitting the counts adds nothing for the credit decision.
